review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the S30ShellLaw section, the S30HypWeight section and `solution`. The two clearest repetitions are in `solution`, where hA and hB do the same log comparison, and between `shell_law` and `solution`, which both prove the same ideleNorm-to-logNorm set identity. Other parallel blocks are short or only look alike: e10 and e11 in `rowMaxNorm_scalar_shape_mul`; harch and hfin in `adelicHeight_scalar_shape_mul`, which target different places and use different entry lemmas; and the smul-formula rewrites for `happ` and `h1` in `shell_law`. findings.problem: hA and hB repeat the same log-comparison argument. Each rewrites an adelic height with the diagOne lemma, substitutes `hθn`, and takes logs of `exp R < p * h` using `Real.log_lt_log_iff` and `Real.log_exp`. Each then splits the log with `Real.log_mul`, `Real.log_pow` (and `Real.log_inv` in hB), clears the division by e, unfolds `logNorm`, and finishes with `constructor <;> intro h <;> linarith`. The two blocks differ only in the factor (`n^e` versus `(n^e)⁻¹`) and in the direction of the comparison. Both are inlined in one long proof, so the shared step is hard to see and any change has to be made twice.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma before `solution`: `theorem exp_lt_mul_iff_log {R p h : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hh : 0 < h) : Real.exp R < p * h ↔ R - Real.log h < Real.log p`. Prove it with `rw [← Real.log_lt_log_iff (Real.exp_pos R) (mul_pos hp hh), Real.log_exp, Real.log_mul hp.ne' hh.ne']; constructor <;> intro <;> linarith`. A second lemma could turn `(ideleNorm y ^ e)` into `e * logNorm y` for `hn : 0 < ideleNorm y`, via `Real.log_pow` and `Real.log_inv`. Then hA becomes: rewrite with the diagOne lemma and `hθn`, apply `exp_lt_mul_iff_log (pow_pos hn e) h₁pos`, rewrite `Real.log_pow`, and close with `div_lt_iff₀`/`linarith`. hB does the same with `inv_pos.mpr (pow_pos hn e)`, `Real.log_inv` and `lt_div_iff₀`. Only the final linear step stays separate.
findings.benefit: The height-versus-log threshold step is stated and proved once. `solution` then only has to say that hA and hB are the two instances of that lemma, with `β` and `α` as the thresholds. This also removes the duplicated positivity side goals and the long `Real.log_*` rewrite chains.

findings.problem: Two proofs establish the same fact: `ideleNorm y ∈ Icc a b` for positive endpoints is equivalent to `logNorm y ∈ Icc (log a) (log b)`. The set equality that follows from this, `Ω ∩ {ideleNorm ∈ Icc a b} = logNorm ⁻¹' Icc (log a) (log b) ∩ Ω`, is proved twice. `shell_law` proves it in the forward direction with `Real.log_le_log_iff`. `solution` (lines 487-493) proves the reverse form with `a = exp α` and `b = exp β`, using the `Real.le_log_iff_exp_le` / `Real.log_le_iff_le_exp` lemmas. Both blocks use the same skeleton: `Set.inter_comm`, `congr 1`, `ext y`, then `ideleNorm_pos y`, then a `simp only` with the log/exp iff lemmas. `solution` then has to undo the log with `Real.log_exp` rewrites at h.
findings.proposed_change: Inside `S30ShellLaw`, add `theorem inter_ideleNorm_Icc_eq (Ω : Set (AdeleRing (𝓞 M) M)ˣ) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) : Ω ∩ {y | NumberField.TateGlobal.ideleNorm M y ∈ Set.Icc a b} = logNorm M ⁻¹' Set.Icc (Real.log a) (Real.log b) ∩ Ω`. Its proof is the current `hset` body from `shell_law`. In `shell_law`, use `rw [measureReal_def, inter_ideleNorm_Icc_eq Ω ha hb, …]`. In `solution`, take `inter_ideleNorm_Icc_eq ΩM (Real.exp_pos α) (Real.exp_pos β)`, then `Real.log_exp`, and use `hS` to turn `S ∩ ΩM` into the `ΩM ∩ {…}` form. This replaces the local `hset` there.
findings.benefit: The relation between `ideleNorm` shells and `logNorm` intervals lives in one named lemma, next to `logNorm`, where other users can find it. `solution` no longer re-derives the log/exp case analysis, which is a separate proof that has to be kept in sync with the one in `shell_law`.
